hints.title: Non-Zero Column Shift
hints.text: From cell (r, c), you can move to any cell in the next row whose column is distinct from c.

hints.title: Maintain Top Two Minimums
hints.text: From the previous row, only the smallest and second smallest costs matter. If column c matches the smallest column, take the second smallest.

hints.title: Linear Row Transition
hints.text: For each row, find the two smallest values and their column indices. Compute the new row DP in linear time.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minFallingPathSum(self, grid: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        n = len(grid)
        first_min, first_col = 0, -1
        second_min = 0
        for row in grid:
            cur_first_min, cur_first_col = float("inf"), -1
            cur_second_min = float("inf")
            for c in range(n):
                prev = second_min if c == first_col else first_min
                val = row[c] + prev
                if val < cur_first_min:
                    cur_second_min = cur_first_min
                    cur_first_min = val
                    cur_first_col = c
                elif val < cur_second_min:
                    cur_second_min = val
            first_min, first_col = cur_first_min, cur_first_col
            second_min = cur_second_min
        return first_min
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all previous row columns for every cell takes cubic time O(N^3).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking the two smallest values in the previous row eliminates redundant column scans.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate optimizes from O(N^3) to O(N^2) using the top two minimum values.
complexity.notes: Constant extra space by just tracking min1, col1, min2 across row transitions.
